headline: Town boards split on Special Town Meeting warrant articles, while municipal departments prepared for service reductions under potential budget override failure scenarios.
synopsis: Ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting, town boards took diverging positions on major warrant articles, with the Advisory Committee recommending against two-family zoning and Community Preservation Act funding for golf irrigation and a trail footbridge, while the Select Board endorsed the zoning and golf articles but rejected the bridge. Multiple municipal departments modeled FY28 budget scenarios, warning that an override failure would trigger staff hour reductions, subscription losses, and program eliminations in the library, health, and conservation departments. Four school committees approved a 22,750 dollar salary adjustment for Superintendent Gregory Martineau and paused a student cell phone geofencing app at Algonquin Regional High School. The Conservation Commission also voted to ask the Select Board to preserve 100,000 dollars in borrowing authorization for Breakneck Hill Farm restoration rather than rescinding it at Town Meeting.

highlights.title: Town boards split on Special Town Meeting warrant articles
highlights.why: The Select Board recommended approval of two-family zoning amendments and golf course irrigation while voting against a trail footbridge. The Advisory Committee voted against recommending all three of those proposals, though both bodies endorsed transitioning the town clerk to an appointed office and creating a stormwater enterprise fund.

highlights.title: Superintendent salary adjustment approved and cell phone app paused
highlights.why: Four school committees approved a 22,750 dollar market salary adjustment for Superintendent Gregory Martineau, bringing his base salary to 270,213 dollars. The regional committee also placed the rollout of the Doorman geofencing mobile app on indefinite hold due to privacy concerns and technical issues.
highlights.body: Northborough School Committee, Southborough School Committee, Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee, and Superintendency Union No. 3

highlights.title: Departments plan severe cuts under potential override failure
highlights.why: Under guidance from town administration, departments prepared two budget scenarios for FY28. If a planned town-wide tax override fails, the library would eliminate programming and cut subscriptions, while the Board of Health and Conservation Commission would be forced to cut staff hours.

highlights.title: Trails Committee mounts campaign after warrant rejections
highlights.why: After both the Select Board and the Advisory Committee voted not to support 217,318 dollars in supplemental CPA funding for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge, the Trails Committee discussed public outreach and weighed asking Town Meeting to extend the expiration date on existing appropriated funds.

highlights.title: Conservation Commission seeks to preserve restoration borrowing
highlights.why: The commission voted 4-1 to ask the Select Board to preserve 100,000 dollars of unissued borrowing capacity from the Breakneck Hill Farm dump cleanup rather than rescinding the full balance at Town Meeting, aiming to fund upcoming site restoration and soil work.
